Author: @nolanc9344
Comment:
Vinegar is acetic acid (typically 5% w/v or weight by volume) and any drink that has been carbonated is carbonic acid. Carbonic acid is stronger than acetic acid, so why isn’t it more effective at cleaning rust? This is because carbonic acid is unstable, and is mostly actually carbon dioxide at any given moment. Therefore, if you had lab-grade carbonic acid, and lab-grade acetic acid at equal concentrations, carbonic acid would be more effective. Basically, the vinegar works better because it is more stable than the acid present in fizzy drinks!
